historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (30.6%) diverges materially from 5yr (7.2%) due to volatile buyback activity and capital structure changes. Equity CAGR not used as primary anchor. Revenue and FCF CAGRs are consistent (15-18% range) and are used as the blended base. FY2026 management guidance midpoint of ~€38B (16.4% growth) used as Year 1 anchor.

valuation_philosophy: This model uses a conservative FCF-based DCF anchored to ASML's confirmed FY2026 guidance and 2030 management targets. ASML's monopoly position in EUV lithography justifies a premium multiple, but the model deliberately does not embed current market sentiment (55x forward P/E) into the terminal value assumptions. Terminal growth of 3% base reflects a normalised long-run rate for a technology infrastructure leader. The gap between intrinsic value and market price is explicitly noted as a sanity check output for the user.

base.description: FY2026 guidance midpoint ~€38B achieved, growth decelerates toward 2030 target midpoint ~€52B, FCF margin stable near FY2025 levels
base.rationale: Year 1 growth 16.4% anchored to management guidance midpoint €38B (from €32.7B FY2025). Decelerates 13%/10%/8%/6% as the China headwind is absorbed and capital intensity stabilises. FCF margin 34% reflects FY2025 actual of 33.8% and assumes modest improvement from IBM mix. WACC 10% = rf 4.2% + beta 1.25 * ERP 4.6% + 0.05 country risk, rounded. Terminal growth 3% = nominal global semiconductor long-run growth.

bull.description: AI supercycle sustains, High-NA EUV ramp accelerates, revenue reaches top of 2030 target range (~€60B), FCF margins expand as High-NA mix improves
bull.rationale: Revenue hits top of FY2026 guidance (€40B) in Year 1 then compounds at 18%/15%/12%/10% toward the €60B 2030 ceiling. FCF margin 38% reflects High-NA ASP tailwind (~€400M vs €200M for Low-NA), expanded IBM contribution, and 56-60% gross margin trajectory by 2030. WACC 9% reflects de-risked technology lead; 4% terminal growth accounts for semiconductor TAM expansion from AI-intensive chip architectures.

bear.description: MATCH Act passes eliminating remaining China DUV revenue, export control allegation lingers, capex cycle peaks in 2026, margin pressured by High-NA ramp costs
bear.rationale: Only 6% growth in Year 1 — China revenue drops from 33% to ~15% rather than guided 20%, MATCH Act passes eliminating remaining DUV China sales, service revenues impacted. FCF margin compressed to 26% as High-NA ramp costs dominate and operational leverage fails to materialise. WACC 12% reflects elevated geopolitical risk premium (EUV diversion allegation, FDPR threat). Terminal growth 2% = pessimistic long-run assumption if EUV competitive disruption occurs beyond 2030.

sensitivity.note: Matrix shows base-case FCF trajectory intrinsic value per share across WACC (rows, 8-12%) and terminal growth rate (columns, 2-4%). All EUR values; USD = EUR x 1.139. Current price €1,576 ($1,795) is above every cell in this matrix.

probability_weighted.rationale: Equal 25/50/25 split given elevated June 2026 uncertainty: EUV diversion allegation unresolved, MATCH Act pending, but AI capex supercycle remains structurally supportive. Bull weighting not raised above 25% given the binary regulatory risk. Bear weighting at 25% reflects genuine tail risk from potential FDPR application (existential scenario for ASML's US-technology-dependent supply chain).

key_metrics.note: Forward P/E based on est. FY2026 EPS ~€28.55 (€38B revenue at 29% net margin / 386M shares). Trailing P/E uses FY2025 EPS €24.73. Market cap computed as 385.7M shares x $1,794.62 / 1.139.

sanity_check.reason: Base case intrinsic value (€603 / $687) implies 24.4x trailing P/E and 20.6x EV/FCF — both within ASML's historical range. The model's assumptions are internally consistent. However, the current market price implies 55x forward P/E and 54.6x EV/FCF, which embeds significant growth and multiple expansion that a standard DCF at normalised discount rates does not support. The large gap between IV and market price reflects the market pricing a structural monopoly premium and AI-cycle optionality not captured by a conservative FCF model.

warning_banner.message: Current price ($1,795 / €1,576) is 61.7% above base-case DCF intrinsic value ($687) and above every cell in the sensitivity matrix. The stock trades at 55x forward P/E vs. a DCF-implied 24x. ASML's monopoly premium and AI cycle positioning may justify a structural valuation above DCF fair value — but the margin of safety is negative at current levels. All scenarios show negative upside on a pure DCF basis.

summary.investment_thesis: ASML is the world's only supplier of EUV lithography with a monopoly backed by 30+ years and $9B+ in cumulative R&D. FY2025 delivered record results (€32.7B revenue, €9.6B net income, €11.0B FCF). FY2026 guidance raised to €36-40B. High-NA EUV ramp is commercially validated. The AI semiconductor supercycle is the primary demand driver through 2030.
summary.valuation_assessment: At $1,794.62 (€1,576), ASML trades at 55x forward P/E and 54.6x EV/FCF — materially above the DCF-derived base case of $687 (€603). The probability-weighted intrinsic value is $729 (€640), implying -59% downside on a pure fundamental basis. The stock's premium reflects monopoly positioning, structural AI demand, and a 30+ year technology lead that markets are willing to pay a significant premium to own. For investors targeting a 15% CAGR to terminal value, the entry price in the bull case is $773, with the base case entry at $397.
summary.primary_risks: June 2026 EUV diversion allegation by US Commerce (ASML denies; FDPR tail risk). MATCH Act pending (could eliminate ~5% of revenue). China revenue declining from 33% to ~20% in FY2026. Semiconductor capex cycle risk post-2027. High-NA EUV ramp execution risk on gross margin path to 56-60% by 2030.
summary.recommendation: OVERVALUED vs. DCF intrinsic value across all scenarios and all sensitivity matrix cells. Current levels price in a combination of monopoly premium, AI cycle optionality, and continued High-NA margin expansion not captured by normalised FCF discounting. Investors who believe in the structural monopoly case and are comfortable with 55x earnings valuations may hold — but no margin of safety exists. New positions at current prices require a very high conviction on both AI capex sustainability and regulatory resolution.
